costGuide.title: Land Rover 306DT Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a Land Rover 306DT engine typically takes 15-20 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent specialist) due to the tight engine bay packaging of the L319 and L494 chassis, and the complexity of the twin-turbo and ancillary systems .
paragraphs: The final Land Rover 306DT engine cost depends heavily on the condition of the bottom end. Because this engine is prone to crankshaft bearing fatigue, sourcing a reconditioned unit with a freshly machined block, new upgraded bearings, and a replaced oil pump is the most cost-effective long-term solution. For a detailed breakdown of what influences these figures across different conditions, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Land Rover 306DT Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Crankshaft Bearing Failure - All 306DT variants
items.whatHappens: The tin-aluminium coating on the crankshaft bearings is susceptible to fatigue and flaking under high load or if oil change intervals are extended. This leads to a loss of oil pressure, a distinct knocking sound from the bottom end on cold starts, and eventually catastrophic engine seizure.
items.repairVsReplace: Once bearing knock is present, the damage is usually widespread. A full reconditioned Land Rover 306DT engine replacement with a machined block and new bearings is the only reliable fix; a simple bearing swap rarely holds long-term.

items.title: Oil Pump and Turbo Contamination - All 306DT variants
items.whatHappens: As the crankshaft bearings degrade, metal swarf circulates through the oil system. This debris frequently blocks the oil pickup strainer, starves the twin turbochargers of lubrication, and causes simultaneous turbo failure.
items.repairVsReplace: If the turbos have failed due to oil starvation, replacing them without addressing the root cause (the bottom end) will result in rapid repeat failure. A full engine replacement is required to guarantee reliability.

failures.goodYearsLine: While the 306DT is a refined and powerful unit, the underlying bearing design flaw persists across all production years. Strict adherence to 5,000-mile oil change intervals and regular oil analysis from 80,000 miles is the only documented way to mitigate the risk .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 306DT
variants.intro: As a Specific page type with no distinct sub-codes listed in the inventory, this section focuses on accurate identification and avoiding common, costly misidentifications. The 306DT engine code is stamped on the engine block and is also recorded on your vehicle’s V5C registration document under "Engine Number". Owners frequently confuse the 306DT with its predecessor, the 276DT, or its successors, the 30DDTX and the AJ20D6. While the 276DT and 306DT share a similar architectural lineage, the 306DT features a different oil pump housing design, twin turbochargers, and a different engine management system. They are not directly interchangeable without significant modifications. Furthermore, the modern 30DDTX and AJ20D6 are entirely different, updated JLR designs (the latter being an inline-six) that will not physically fit the Discovery 4 or early Range Rover Sport L494 chassis without extensive modification.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 306DT - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Land Rover 306DT engine for sale can be a budget-friendly option, but it carries a severe inherent risk. Unless the seller can provide comprehensive service records proving strict, 5,000-mile oil changes and a recent compression or oil pressure test, you are likely inheriting a ticking time bomb of bearing wear. Learn more about used engines.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: For most owners, a reconditioned Land Rover 306DT is the only sensible choice. A proper recon will proactively address the engine’s known weaknesses by machining the block, fitting upgraded crankshaft bearings, replacing the oil pump, and installing new twin turbochargers, delivering near-new reliability for the future. Explore reconditioned engine options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for low-mileage, high-spec Discovery 4 or Range Rover Sport projects where the engine is being stripped to the bare block. This allows for line-boring the main bearings, balancing the rotating assembly, and ensuring the engine matches the pristine condition of the flagship chassis. View rebuilt engine services.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting your replacement through our vetted network ensures the work is completed by specialists familiar with Land Rover's complex twin-turbo diesel systems, backed by a nationwide warranty. Check supply and fit availability.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Discovery 4 and Range Rover Sport L494 models typically hold values between £10,000 and £40,000, depending on mileage, specification, and condition . While a reconditioned replacement is generally financially viable for these premium hosts, it is still crucial to evaluate the vehicle's overall body condition and service history before committing to a major mechanical investment. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value first.

items.answer: A reconditioned Land Rover 306DT engine typically costs between £6,500 and £9,500 for supply only, with fitted prices ranging from £7,475 to £10,800. items.question: What is the most common failure on the Land Rover 306DT engine?
items.answer: The most critical failure on the 306DT is crankshaft bearing fatigue, where the tin-aluminium coating flakes under load or extended oil intervals. This leads to a loss of oil pressure, a distinct bottom-end knock on cold starts, and eventual engine seizure. As bearings degrade, metal swarf circulates through the oil system, frequently destroying the oil pump and twin turbochargers. Once bearing knock is present, a full reconditioned replacement with a machined block is the only reliable fix.

items.question: Which Land Rover models use the 306DT engine?
items.answer: The 306DT twin-turbo diesel was fitted to the Land Rover Discovery 4 and Range Rover Sport (L494) between 2009 and 2016. It served as the primary diesel powerplant for these premium SUVs, offering 245-292 hp depending on the TDV6 or SDV6 tune. It replaced the older 2.7-litre V6 and was eventually succeeded by updated V6 and inline-six architectures.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 306DT engine?
items.answer: For any Discovery 4 or Range Rover Sport, a reconditioned 306DT is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the high risk of bottom-end failure. Used engines almost always inherit the same crankshaft bearing fatigue or oil pump contamination that caused the original removal. A proper reconditioned build machines the block, fits upgraded bearings, and replaces the oil pump and turbos to guarantee reliability. Reconditioned units also include comprehensive compression and oil pressure testing.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the 306DT engine?
items.answer: You can confirm your engine code by checking the V5C registration document under the "Engine Number" field or by locating the code stamped on the engine block. The 306DT is a 3.0-litre V6 twin-turbo diesel, easily distinguished from the older 2.7L V6 or the modern Ingenium inline-six. Fitting a 2.7L wiring loom or ECU to a 306DT block will result in incorrect fueling and poor drivability. Both the 2.7L and 3.0L share the Lion V6 architecture, but they are not direct plug-and-play swaps due to displacement and turbo differences.
